title: Dover Fueling Solutions Launches ProGauge MagLink Anywhere for Mobile Automatic Tank Gauge Data Access
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- Dover Fueling Solutions ("DFS"), a part of Dover (NYSE: DOV) and a leading global provider of advanced customer-focused technologies, services...
body_text: DOWNERS GROVE, Ill. , July 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dover Fueling Solutions ("DFS") , a part of Dover (NYSE: DOV ) and a leading global provider of advanced customer-focused technologies, services and solutions in the fuel and convenience retail industries, today announced the launch of ProGauge MagLink Anywhere™, a new automatic tank gauge (ATG) mobile app designed to give fuel retailers reliable, real-time access to critical tank and console data. As fuel retailers look to improve inventory control and make faster decisions across sites, access to accurate tank data is becoming increasingly important. Available globally, MagLink Anywhere provides retailers a clearer view of their fuel retail business, while strengthening the connectivity between various site ecosystems. The app works seamlessly with existing ProGauge® consoles, including the ProGauge MagLink LX 4® console, ProGauge MagLink LX Plus® console, and ProGauge MagLink LX Ultimate® console. By bringing fuel station and underground tank data into a single mobile view, MagLink Anywhere gives retailers quick access to the information they need to monitor inventory, review site activity, and respond to issues requiring attention as they occur. "Fuel retailers generate vast amounts of operational data every day but turning that information into actionable insights has long been a challenge," said Nuno Almeida, DFS Product Management Director. "With MagLink Anywhere, we're putting powerful intelligence directly into the hands of operators, enabling them to monitor inventory, identify issues sooner, and make smarter decisions from anywhere, at any time, and through an easy-to-use platform." MagLink Anywhere allows the end user to pair to their ProGauge console easily and quickly, using a secure architecture that safeguards data transmitted through the app and supports controls intended to limit unauthorized access. Fergus Heading, DFS ATG Business Development Director, added, "We designed the app to improve time management, enhance visibility into console and tank data, and provide stability within overall business operations. Whether operating a single site or managing a large network of tank gauging equipment, MagLink Anywhere gives fuel retailers a practical way to access the inventory and site information they need in one place." To learn more information about the MagLink Anywhere app, visit ProGauge MagLink Anywhere . About Dover Fueling Solutions: Dover Fueling Solutions® (DFS) is part of Dover Corporation and a leading provider of advanced energy dispensing equipment, electronic automation, point-of-sale and payment systems, automatic tank gauging and subscription solutions to fueling and convenience retail customers worldwide. Comprised of brands Wayne®, Tokheim®, OPW®, ProGauge®, Fairbanks®, AvaLAN Networks™, LIQAL®, Bulloch Technologies®, and SiteIQ™, DFS is dedicated to offering a broad range of solutions that power vehicles, including conventional fuel and clean energy products that support gasoline, diesel, bio-diesel and ethanol as well as LNG, H2, LPG, CNG and EV chargers. Headquartered in Austin, TX, DFS has a strong global manufacturing and technology development presence, including facilities in Brazil, Canada, China, India, Italy, Poland, Belgium, the Netherlands, the United Kingdom and the United States. For more information about DFS, visit www.doverfuelingsolutions.com . About Dover: Dover is a diversified global manufacturer and solutions provider with annual revenue of over $8 billion. We deliver innovative equipment and components, consumable supplies, aftermarket parts, software and digital solutions, and support services through five operating segments: Engineered Products, Clean Energy & Fueling, Imaging & Identification, Pumps & Process Solutions and Climate & Sustainability Technologies. Dover combines global scale with operational agility to lead the markets we serve. Recognized for our entrepreneurial approach for over 70 years, our team of approximately 24,000 employees takes an ownership mindset, collaborating with customers to redefine what's possible. Headquartered in Downers Grove, Illinois, Dover trades on the New York Stock Exchange under "DOV." Additional information is available at dovercorporation.com . title: How JustAI uses reinforcement learning to power AI marketing
summary: At JustAI, we’ve built an AI-first decisioning platform that continuously learns and adapts, in real time, using reinforcement learning (RL) and large language model (LLM) optimization. This means better personalization, faster learning cycles, and measurable lift without additional manual testing overhead.
body_text: Modern marketing moves too fast for slow, one-off experiments. Campaign performance changes daily, audiences shift weekly, and new creative ideas drop constantly. If your optimization strategy can’t keep up, you’re leaving money on the table. At Just Words, we’ve built an AI-first decisioning platform that continuously learns and adapts , in real time, using reinforcement learning (RL) and large language model (LLM) optimization. This means better personalization, faster learning cycles, and measurable lift without additional manual testing overhead. The Core Problem: Exploration vs. Exploitation Marketers face the classic multi-armed bandit problem : Exploitation: Show the best-known message, based on past performance, to maximize short-term results. Exploration: Test new or less-proven ideas to uncover tomorrow’s winners. Traditional A/B testing fixes traffic splits and runs for weeks. That’s fine for academic experiments, but in the real world it: Misses short-term opportunities when a creative starts winning mid-test. Fails to adapt when audience behavior changes. Treats all audiences the same , ignoring differences in context. We solve this with two complementary RL approaches: 1. Weighted Thompson Sampling - Statistical Optimization WTS is our default scorer for campaigns where audiences are well-defined and we care about global winners. How it works: Bayesian Modeling: Each creative’s success rate is modeled as a Beta(α, β) distribution, updated as we see opens, clicks, or conversions. Multi-Metric Weighting: We can blend multiple metrics (open rate, CTR, downstream conversions) into a single weighted score. Bias Correction: Median-based adjustments normalize performance across campaigns with different baselines. Graceful Degradation: Neutral priors ensure that sparse data doesn’t cause wild swings. When to use it: Best for global campaigns or well-segmented lists where creative performance is relatively stable. 2. Disjoint Linear Thompson Sampling- Contextual Optimization DLTS is a contextual bandit , it doesn’t just learn which creative is best overall; it learns which creative is best for this user right now . How it works: Feature Encoding: Compress user attributes and campaign context into a high-dimensional vector (e.g., user type, lifecycle stage, device, time of day). Per-Variant Models: Each creative variant gets its own linear model: Reward ≈ θᵀx + noise Bayesian Updates: We maintain uncertainty in each model’s parameters using normal-inverse-gamma priors. Posterior Sampling: For each decision, we sample from the posterior to balance exploration and exploitation. When to use it: High-cardinality or high-variability campaigns, e.g., the same subject line might perform differently for SMB vs. enterprise, or for morning vs. evening sends. 3. Auto-Tune for LLM Optimization - Closing the Loop Picking the right creative variant is only half the story. We also need to generate new, high-performing ideas, without human bottlenecks. That’s where Just Words Auto-Tune comes in. The Challenge: Even the smartest bandit will plateau if the creative pool never changes. Manually crafting new variants is slow, and guessing what will work is risky. Our Solution: We use LLMs to automatically generate and refine content, guided by live performance data from our bandit models. How it works: Performance Feedback Loop: The RL layer sends “winning patterns” to the LLM — e.g., tone, length, keywords, emotional framing that are over-indexing. Prompt Engineering with Guardrails: We feed the LLM structured prompts with brand voice, compliance rules, and campaign goals. Controlled Variant Generation: Auto-Tune produces new candidates that differ enough to explore, but stay on-brand and compliant. Live Testing: New variants are inserted into the bandit’s pool for real-time evaluation. Iterative Refinement: The process repeats — only better-performing styles survive. Result: Continuous creative evolution, fully automated, with the bandit + LLM working as a closed-loop optimization engine. Why This Matters for Marketing, Data, and Eng Teams For Marketing: No more waiting weeks to declare a winner. Messaging adapts to audience segments automatically. Creative refreshes happen continuously without manual effort. For Data: True causal lift measurement in production. Multi-metric scoring aligns optimization with business goals. Contextual models capture non-obvious audience behaviors. For Engineering: Sub-100ms decision latency in production. Scalable to millions of daily decisions. Modular architecture supports plugging in new scoring strategies or content generators. The Impact in Production Across millions of daily content decisions, our RL + Auto-Tune system has delivered: Double-digit engagement lifts vs. static control groups. Faster time-to-winner - often hours instead of weeks. Higher creative diversity without off-brand risk. It’s marketing experimentation on autopilot, but with the rigor of data science and the scale of modern engineering.

title: Durham Townhome and Condo Living: A Buyer’s Guide
summary: Explore condo and townhome living in Durham, NC, including costs, HOA rules, insurance, and resale tips so you can buy with confidence. Contact us.
body_text: Wondering whether a Durham condo or townhome is the right move for you? If you want lower-maintenance living, a more in-town location, or a price point that can differ from detached homes, attached housing can be a smart option. The key is knowing how ownership, monthly costs, and association rules work before you buy. Let’s dive in. Why condos and townhomes matter in Durham Durham has made room for attached housing as part of its long-term growth. The city’s Comprehensive Plan identifies Apartment and Townhouse Neighborhoods as a formal place type and says these residential areas should be found throughout Durham. That planning approach lines up with what many buyers want today. Durham’s Expanding Housing Choices initiative notes that fast population growth, limited developable land, and a renewed preference for in-town living have all contributed to housing availability and affordability challenges. For you as a buyer, that helps explain why condos and townhomes remain an important part of the local market. Where you may see attached housing in Durham Attached housing appears in several parts of Durham, often in areas tied to compact-neighborhood or transit-oriented planning. City planning materials point to places such as Leigh Village, Patterson Place, South Square and MLK Jr. Parkway, Erwin Road near Duke University and the VA Medical Center, and Alston Avenue. In Southside, just south of downtown and north of NCCU, the city describes a redevelopment area of about 125 acres that includes homes, apartment communities, and commercial development. Southside phases have included townhouses and live-work apartments, which shows how attached housing fits into Durham’s evolving urban fabric. Around Erwin Road, the city describes a dense mixed-use area with large multi-family apartment complexes, many built between the 1970s and 2000s. The city also notes an area north of University Drive and west of MLK Jr. Parkway with apartment and townhome communities generally built around 1990, with nearby redevelopment focused around South Square, Parkway Plaza, and West Gate. Condo vs. townhome ownership Before you compare listings, it helps to understand what you are actually buying. A condo and a townhome can look similar from the outside, but the ownership structure can be very different. How a condo is owned Under North Carolina’s Condominium Act, each condo unit and its interest in the common elements is a separate parcel of real estate. Each unit is also separately taxed and assessed. In a condo community, the association can adopt budgets, collect assessments for common expenses, regulate common elements, and maintain, repair, or replace common elements. In practical terms, that often means the association takes on more responsibility for shared structures and common areas. How a townhome is owned Durham’s development ordinance defines a townhouse as a building made up of three or more attached dwelling units on individual lots that share side walls. That legal definition matters because townhome ownership often feels more like owning a small-lot house than owning a condo. Under North Carolina’s Planned Community Act, which covers many newer HOA-governed townhome communities, the association can budget, collect assessments, and regulate common elements. But the owner is generally responsible for the lot and improvements on it unless the declaration says otherwise. Why the difference matters to you This is where many buyers get tripped up. Two attached homes with similar prices can come with very different maintenance responsibilities. A condo often shifts more shared-structure responsibility to the association. A townhome can range from near full owner responsibility to partial exterior maintenance by the association, depending on the community documents. That is why reviewing the declaration, rules, and maintenance responsibilities is so important. Monthly costs to budget for The sticker price is only part of the story. When you buy a Durham condo or townhome, your monthly housing cost usually includes several moving parts. Core monthly expenses You should expect to budget for: Principal and interest on your mortgage Property taxes Homeowners or unit-owner insurance HOA dues Utility bills if they are not covered by the association HOA dues are typically paid separately from the mortgage payment. That means a home that looks affordable at first glance may feel very different once dues and insurance are added in. Durham property taxes Durham’s FY 2026-2027 combined city and county tax rate is $1.0163 per $100 of assessed value. That works out to about $1,016.30 in annual property tax for every $100,000 of value before exemptions. For example, if you are looking at a home assessed at $300,000, the annual property tax at that rate would be about $3,048.90 before any applicable exemptions. That is a useful number to build into your planning early. Utilities and service costs If utilities are not included in your HOA dues, ask for a clear breakdown. Durham water is billed on a tiered usage schedule, and sewer is billed on a flat volume basis with added service charges. The city also notes that customers outside city limits can face higher service charges. Even if a listing looks straightforward, utility structure can still affect your true monthly cost. Insurance for condos and townhomes Insurance is another area where buyers should ask detailed questions. Condo association dues usually include master insurance for common areas, but you still need your own coverage for the unit. Freddie Mac now requires an HO-6 unit-owner policy when the master property policy does not cover all or part of the unit interior or when the master policy includes a per-unit deductible. In simple terms, do not assume the association’s policy covers everything inside your walls. How to evaluate the HOA In condos and townhomes, the association is a big part of what you are buying. Your future costs, maintenance experience, and resale potential can all be affected by how the HOA is run. What the HOA should tell you North Carolina disclosure rules require sellers to disclose whether the property is subject to association rules, the amount of regular dues or assessments, the services paid for by those dues, and any approved special assessments or pending lawsuits involving the association. That gives you a starting point, but it should not be your stopping point. You want to go beyond the summary and understand how the community operates in practice. Smart HOA questions to ask These are some of the most useful questions for buyers: What do the dues cover? How well funded are the reserves? Are any special assessments planned? Is there litigation involving the association? What part of the building is insured by the association versus the owner? Are there rental limits or occupancy restrictions that could affect future marketability? These questions can help you spot both value and risk. A higher monthly HOA fee is not automatically bad if it supports strong reserves, meaningful maintenance coverage, and stable operations. Financing and resale considerations When you buy a condo or townhome, you are not just buying a home. You are also buying into a project or community structure that a future buyer and lender will evaluate later. Fannie Mae’s project review framework looks at legal documents, budgets, financial statements, reserve studies, litigation, and insurance. Freddie Mac also says project review should address marketability, financial stability, litigation, occupancy restrictions, common elements and amenities, and insurance adequacy. One especially important point is reserves. Freddie Mac notes that underfunded reserves can lead to special assessments or higher HOA assessments, which can create financial hardship for owners. For you, that means the health of the association can influence both your monthly costs now and your resale options later. What this means for first-time and relocating buyers If you are buying your first home or moving to Durham from outside the Triangle, a condo or townhome can offer a simpler entry point into the market. You may find options in locations that support a shorter commute, easier access to daily needs, or less exterior upkeep than a detached home. At the same time, attached housing asks you to pay closer attention to the fine print. The right fit is not just about the floor plan or finishes. It is also about ownership structure, dues, insurance, maintenance responsibilities, and how well the association is managed. How to shop smarter in Durham If you are comparing Durham condos and townhomes, it helps to evaluate each one through the same lens. That makes it easier to separate a good fit from a home that only looks appealing on the surface. A practical buyer checklist As you tour homes, keep these points in mind: Confirm whether the home is legally a condo or a townhome Ask what the HOA fee covers and what it does not Review current dues and any approved special assessments Ask about reserves, litigation, and insurance coverage Estimate taxes, insurance, utilities, and dues together Look at the surrounding area and redevelopment context Think about future resale, including buyer and lender appeal This approach can help you make a more confident decision. It also gives you a clearer picture of your real cost of ownership before you get too far into the process. Buying a condo or townhome in Durham can be a great move if you match the home, the community, and the ownership structure to your goals. Whether you are looking for a first home, a lower-maintenance lifestyle, or a practical in-town option, careful due diligence can make all the difference. If you want help comparing communities, reading the details, and finding the right fit in Durham, reach out to Spotlight Realty . FAQs What is the difference between a condo and a townhome in Durham? In general, a condo gives you ownership of your unit plus an interest in common elements, while a townhome is typically an attached home on an individual lot with shared side walls. Maintenance responsibilities can differ a lot based on the community documents. What costs should you budget for with a Durham condo or townhome? You should usually budget for mortgage principal and interest, property taxes, insurance, HOA dues, and any utilities not covered by the association. What do HOA dues usually cover in a Durham attached home community? Coverage varies by community, but dues commonly help pay for shared expenses such as common-area maintenance, landscaping, and association operations. You should always confirm the exact services and responsibilities. Why do HOA reserves matter when buying a Durham condo or townhome? Reserve funding matters because underfunded reserves can lead to higher dues or special assessments, which can affect your monthly budget and future resale. What HOA questions should a Durham condo or townhome buyer ask? Ask what the dues cover, how well funded the reserves are, whether any special assessments are planned, whether there is litigation, what insurance the association carries, and whether rental or occupancy restrictions apply. Where are some Durham areas with condos and townhomes? City planning materials identify attached-housing or compact-neighborhood areas including Leigh Village, Patterson Place, South Square and MLK Jr. Parkway, Erwin Road near Duke and the VA Medical Center, Alston Avenue, and Southside. title: Bobbi Sondreal Joins Alerus as Senior Wealth and Fiduciary Advisor
summary: Alerus is pleased to announce Bobbi Sondreal has joined the company as a senior wealth and fiduciary advisor, based in Grand Forks.
body_text: Back Bobbi Sondreal Joins Alerus as Senior Wealth and Fiduciary Advisor July 29, 2026 Alerus is pleased to announce Bobbi Sondreal has joined the company as a senior wealth and fiduciary advisor, based in Grand Forks. Bobbi is a Certified Trust and Fiduciary Advisor with nearly 20 years of financial services experience, specializing in trust administration and wealth management for high-net-worth individuals and families. She contributes her expertise to help clients navigate complex financial and fiduciary matters, providing personalized guidance, exceptional client service, and regulatory expertise to support their legacy-focused planning. She also works directly with clients, attorneys, CPAs, and other experienced professionals to administer a diverse portfolio of trusts, conservatorships, custodial accounts, IRAs, and estates. Before rejoining Alerus in June 2026, Bobbi served as a succession and retirement officer at AgCountry Farm Credit Services in Grand Forks. She previously spent nine years with Alerus as a member of the wealth management and trust team. She holds a bachelor’s degree in business administration from North Dakota State University. title: Picking Our Spots in a Record Convertible Market
summary: Record convertible issuance and AI infrastructure tailwinds are creating compelling opportunities. Calamos Convertible Fund leverages active management and bottom-up selection to pursue growth companies with favorable risk-reward asymmetry, while convertible structures that offer downside mitigation provide resilience amid persistent geopolitical and macroeconomic uncertainty.
body_text: Picking Our Spots in a Record Convertible Market July 1, 2026 Calamos Convertible Fund (CICVX) Jon Vacko , CFA, and Joe Wysocki , CFA Summary Points: We’re finding many opportunities to invest in exciting growth companies with quality fundamentals and less exposure to downside. We believe that convertibles can be extremely compelling in an environment characterized by transformative secular trends and economic expansion, but also fast-moving, volatile market conditions. We believe active management is the key to unlocking the benefits of the asset class: our focus remains on selecting securities with favorable risk-reward asymmetry and on continuously rebalancing our positions to capitalize on short-term volatility. Equity markets delivered solid gains in the second quarter, with convertible securities participating meaningfully in the advance. The fund’s returns have been strong this year, a result that we believe reflects both the quality of the opportunity set and the benefits of our active management, which has positioned the fund well to navigate a complex and rapidly evolving environment. Although the Middle East conflict wears on, both sides continue to search for an acceptable resolution. A successful de-escalation could lower the geopolitical risk premium, ease oil prices, and provide a meaningful tailwind for consumers and the economy overall. Beneath the geopolitical noise, broader market conditions are constructive: economic growth is solid, overall credit quality is sound, bankruptcy risk is low, and access to capital remains plentiful across IPOs, equity, and debt markets. Within Calamos Convertible Fund (CICVX), our overall focus remains on thematic convictions, bottom-up company selection, and active management of security-specific risk-reward tradeoffs across the portfolio. Our portfolio construction reflects both the durability of the AI theme and our readiness to capture a wider opportunity set should conditions warrant. Information technology and industrials remain the fund’s largest sector overweights, reflecting our view that the AI infrastructure buildout is a structural, multiyear investment cycle. The buildout spans data center construction, power delivery, and connectivity infrastructure. While the debate around AI durability persists, the fundamentals for beneficiaries of the capex infrastructure trend remain exceptional, and the convertible market offers ample opportunities to participate in this theme with favorable asymmetric payoff profiles. Additionally, if geopolitical tensions ease, inflation cools, and economic growth accelerates, we see a potential case for a broadening of market leadership with cyclical companies benefiting from an improved backdrop. New issuance volume has been remarkable, with $137.5 billion coming to market in the first half of the year, well on pace to shatter last year’s record total. As we detailed in our recent post, “ Leaders of Today, Leaders of Tomorrow: Convertible Opportunity in Focus ,” convertibles have historically served as growth capital for growth companies, and the AI buildout provides an ideal backdrop for that dynamic to continue. The recent entry of Alphabet into the convertible market reinforces our view that the asset class offers a unique opportunity to invest in the leaders of today and tomorrow in risk-managed structures. Looking toward the back half of the year, we expect volatility to remain a feature of markets. While midterm elections, geopolitical developments, the ongoing debate over AI’s durability, and Fed policy uncertainty are among the more foreseeable sources of volatility, we expect markets to remain sensitive to a range of developments. We maintain the fund’s emphasis on companies with improving margins and free cash flow, accelerating returns on invested capital, and attractive equity valuations. Owning these companies through convertible structures allows us to pursue that growth with the added benefit of downside mitigation, a combination we believe is particularly valuable when the range of potential outcomes remains wide. title: DEMRE extiende el plazo de inscripción a la PAES Regular hasta el 27 de julio
summary: Debido a la emergencia climática que afectó a Atacama, Coquimbo y Valparaíso, el DEMRE extendió el plazo de inscripción a la PAES Regular 2026 hasta el lunes 27 de julio a las 13:00 horas. Te contamos cómo inscribirte, quiénes están exentos de pago y las fechas clave del proceso.
body_text: De forma excepcional, el DEMRE decidió ampliar el plazo de inscripción a la PAES Regular 2026, Admisión 2027, que originalmente vencía este miércoles 22 de julio. La medida responde a la emergencia climática que afectó a gran parte del país durante los últimos días, especialmente a las regiones de Atacama, Coquimbo y Valparaíso, y busca dar más tiempo a quienes aún no han podido completar su registro. ¿Cuál es el nuevo plazo? El Comité Técnico de Acceso resolvió extender la inscripción por cinco días adicionales. El nuevo plazo máximo es: Lunes 27 de julio, a las 13:00 horas 11:00 horas en Rapa Nui 14:00 horas en Aysén y Magallanes ¿Cómo inscribirse? Quienes aún no hayan efectuado su inscripción o no hayan completado el formulario de registro deben hacerlo lo antes posible ingresando a demre.cl o acceso.mineduc.cl. El proceso incluye: Completar todos los datos requeridos. Seleccionar la sede de rendición. Elegir todas las pruebas a rendir (incluyendo, si corresponde, la prueba electiva o la de Competencia Matemática 2, M2). Descargar la Tarjeta de Identificación. Para quienes tengan dudas sobre el paso a paso, el DEMRE dispone de un instructivo detallado con todas las instrucciones del proceso de inscripción en su sitio web. ¿Tiene costo la inscripción? Sí, el arancel varía según la cantidad de pruebas inscritas. Sin embargo, existen exenciones importantes a través de la Beca PAES : Estudiantes de 4º año medio en colegios municipales, de Servicios Locales de Educación Pública (SLEP), particulares subvencionados y de administración delegada quedan exentos de pago automáticamente. Estudiantes de colegios particulares pagados también pueden acceder al beneficio si acreditan una situación socioeconómica vulnerable ante el Mineduc. ¿Qué prueba electiva elegir? Para quienes aún no deciden qué prueba electiva rendir, o si necesitan la prueba de Competencia Matemática 2 (M2), el DEMRE recomienda revisar la Nómina Preliminar de Carreras, publicación oficial disponible en su sitio web, que detalla los requisitos de cada carrera y universidad. ¿Cuándo se rinde la PAES Regular? La aplicación de la PAES Regular está programada para los días 30 de noviembre, 1 y 2 de diciembre de este año.

title: The Zeigarnik Effect: Why Unfinished Work Hijacks your Mind
summary: Dex turns your browser into a single AI workspace — one brain that knows your tasks, your context, and how to move your work forward.
body_text: It's 2:00 AM, and you've been staring at the ceiling for an hour. Not because of tomorrow's exam—you studied for that, and it's done. You're stuck on the essay that's due next week, the one you've barely started, replaying the introduction paragraph you can't quite get right. What is the Zeigarnik Effect? That's not a distraction; that's just the Zeigarnik effect . Discovered by psychologist Bluma Zeigarnik, the phenomenon describes how unfinished or interrupted tasks create significantly stronger memory traces than completed ones. The brain treats incomplete work as an open cognitive loop, which persists in working memory, creating background mental noise that not only fragments your attention, but drains cognitive resources. It's why cliffhangers work in TV shows, and it's also why you can't mentally clock out even after physically leaving the office. Zeigarnik Effect’s Mental Tax The invisible cognitive debt that you accrue daily from the Zeigarnik effect starts to compound and becomes mental residue that makes you never fully engaged in your current endeavors. The problem is, this effect becomes contagious in enterprise environments. Asynchronous communication creates hundreds of open loops within the workplace, and context switching between projects amplifies this. Beyond the 15-23 minutes of recovery time the brain needs from context switching, your attention is being lost to productivity killers such as decision paralysis. Instead of focusing on meaningful work that seems overwhelming, you procrastinate and gravitate towards trivial busywork that feels controllable. Restructuring Unfinished Tasks The Zeigarnik effect isn't a bug in human cognition—it's a state that you can control intentionally to amplify your productivity rather than drain it. Here’s how: Externalize every open loop immediately; The moment you can't finish something, write down these things: exactly where you left off, your next specific action, and when you'll do it. Create micro-completions inside larger projects; Break down large tasks into bite-sized pieces so that when you finish them, the momentum from these small wins compounds. Batch closure sessions; Aggressively finish, delegate, document, or delete anything incomplete. Treat closure as a skill worth practicing. The Future of Productivity The future of productivity isn't about never leaving things unfinished; It's about managing open loops so intentionally that they work for you instead of against you. Your breakthrough ideas aren't hiding—they're just buried under the weight of 40 things you haven't finished.

title: What 1 hour of downtime actually costs
summary: One hour of downtime can cost $300,000 or more. See costs by industry and learn how businesses can reduce outage risk.
body_text: OOMA Business Blog What 1 hour of downtime actually costs Husain Sumra July 27, 2026 | 4 min read When your systems go offline, everything slows down at once. Calls stop connecting, transactions fail and the workflows your team relies on grind to a halt. Even a short outage can hit your bottom line within minutes. For most businesses, downtime is a direct, measurable hit to revenue and productivity. To help put a number on the problem, the team at Ooma dug into the research and created an infographic that breaks down what downtime really costs across industries and company sizes. The universal baseline cost of an outage The exact price tag on an outage depends on your company’s size and how complex your operations are, but there’s a baseline worth knowing: Ninety percent of mid-sized and large enterprises report that one hour of downtime costs $300,000 or more. For a lot of organizations, that’s a very conservative number. For businesses with highly integrated operations, an hour of downtime can cost more than a house, more than a year of multiple salaries combined or an entire quarter’s marketing spend. In fact, 41 percent of enterprises report losing $1 million to $5 million per hour when systems go down. How the cost of downtime varies by industry How much an outage hurts usually comes down to one thing: how tightly your network uptime is tied to your revenue and your production line. Finance and banking: High-frequency trading and nonstop transaction processing mean costs add up fast here. Losses range from $1 million to more than $5 million per hour, or roughly $83,333 per minute. Auto manufacturing: Assembly lines depend on tight synchronization, so when systems go down, so does production. That can run about $2.3 million per hour, or more than $38,000 per minute. Retail and e-commerce: If your storefront is offline, customers can’t check out. That’s direct revenue loss, typically $1 million to $2 million per hour. Health IT and data centers: Health organizations see costs around $474,000 per hour during downtime, while standard data center outages land between $300,000 and $540,000 per hour. Why downtime gets so expensive The cost of an outage rarely stays in one department. It tends to compound across three areas: Lost revenue: When your systems are down, customers can’t buy, pay or interact with your business at all. Operational disruption: Even when revenue isn’t directly on the line, the bills keep coming. Your team, your systems and your production lines sit idle, which means you’re still paying for labor and overhead with nothing to show for it. Recovery and compliance costs: Once you’re back online, the cleanup begins, including remediation work, possible regulatory penalties and reputational damage. In regulated industries, an outage can trigger compliance violations on top of everything else. Stop the clock: Mitigating the impact of downtime You can’t prevent every outage, but you can keep a small incident from turning into an expensive one with the right plan in place. Data backup: Regularly duplicate critical data in a secondary environment, so you’ve always got a copy ready before hardware fails or a security incident hits. Failover systems: A secondary connection that automatically reroutes traffic keeps things running when a server or network goes down locally. Business continuity: A solid continuity plan keeps your core operations going even if your primary facility or network is out of commission. Crisis communication: Clear status pages, email and text messages keep customers and employees in the loop during a disruption and help preserve their trust. Recovery plans: A streamlined recovery protocol gets your services back online faster, which shortens the outage and limits the financial damage. The ROI of uninterrupted connectivity The numbers make it clear: Network downtime is a real financial risk. With the cost rising to hundreds of thousands of dollars an hour or more for most enterprises, the real question isn’t whether you can afford to invest in failover solutions: It’s whether you can afford not to. Put business continuity measures and redundant infrastructure in place now and you can protect your revenue, keep customers’ trust and stop a minor hardware glitch from turning into a multimillion-dollar problem. That’s exactly what Ooma’s business communication solutions are built for: reliable connections that keep your business running no matter what. If you’re ready to see what that looks like for your team, explore our VoIP phone plans and 5G business internet service today. Frequently asked questions What is a network failover system? A failover system is a backup plan that automatically switches your network or communication traffic to a secondary connection the moment your primary connection fails or runs into trouble. How much downtime is acceptable for a business? The answer depends on the organization, but many businesses aim for at least 99.9 percent uptime. Even that allows nearly nine hours of downtime per year, which can become costly for organizations that rely on continuous customer access or real-time operations. What are the most common causes of downtime? Common causes include internet service outages, hardware failures, software bugs, cyberattacks, power disruptions, human error and third-party service failures. Many outages result from a combination of factors rather than a single event.
